summary: Mined the ledger (274 review_outcomes, 220 gate_discriminations, 187 modifier_attempts, 21 cell_failures, 8 accept_decisions, 569 seat_teardowns, 1879 gate_results) plus the 104,982-line JSONL and, because neither records finding kinds, the 339 reviewer ReturnEnvelopes on disk (254 typed findings). Headline: must_fix >= 1 is equivalent to changes-needed on 273/274 rows, so the counts restate the verdict and carry no defect kind; 35.1% of 194 lanes bounce at review round 1 (68/194), 52% of reviews with a findings array find nothing (140/269), and the gate is green while review still finds a must-fix in 65 of 188 runs (34.6%). Strongest rubric discriminator measured: a finding that opens by naming a concrete triggering state is must-fix 95/129 (74%) vs 25/125 (20%); doc/prose, out-of-plan and carried-forward findings are 0 must-fix in 23, 5 and 10 respectively; the highest-VOLUME class (vacuous tests / surviving mutations, 46/254) is below baseline at 24% must-fix. gate_discriminations has exactly one unproven row in 220 and it is an infra refusal with NULL check counts, so the brief's 'what does a discrimination failure look like' is an honest gap; the proof that actually fires is the per-check mutation pass (1102 applied, 9 survivors). modifier_attempts: 187 attempts produced 3 real cell changes (155 refused as pane-transport). Register at task/findings.md with every query, denominator and confound named; 12 queries preserved under task/queries/. Zero files changed in the checkout (git status --porcelain empty); the ledger was opened readOnly throughout and the CLI verbs were re-implemented rather than invoked, to avoid openLedger's read-write open.

findings.summary: STRUCTURAL: the ledger records review VOLUME, never review CONTENT -- and the JSONL is not richer. A recordReviewOutcome JSONL record carries exactly the db row's fields {adw_id, phase_id, dispatch_id, role, verdict, must_fix, should_fix, consider, created_at} and no finding text. The machine-readable corpus therefore covers 92 of 124 (74%) of the disk's changes-needed envelopes. Direct consequence of crew/roles/reviewer.md:49 making `findings` optional.

findings.summary: Strongest single discriminator found: a finding whose summary OPENS by naming a concrete triggering state ('A ...', 'With ...', 'When ...', 'Passing/Omitting/Deleting ...') is must-fix 95/129 (74%) versus 25/125 (20%) for one that does not -- a 3.7x separation. Runner-up arms: indeterminate-collapsed-to-definite 57% (n=44), test/gate-file location 36% (n=53), cites own measurement 33% (n=21), proves a mutation survives 28% (n=25), names a plan divergence 25% (n=20).

findings.summary: Severity is INVERSELY correlated with length, so F10 is not a verbosity proxy: must-fix median 143 chars (mean 158, n=120), should-fix 284 (257, n=51), consider 273 (273, n=83). A real defect states itself in one short sentence; a consider takes a hedged paragraph. Mechanically checkable as a rubric rule.

findings.summary: Prose, conformance and carried-forward findings have NEVER bounced a lane. Four disjoint instruments all return zero must-fix: location is a .md/README file 0/16; summary is about a stale comment/prose claim 0/7; explicitly carried forward from a prior round 0/10; classifier stale-prose + out-of-plan 0/23; docs/ + docs/adr/ 0/8. crew/roles/reviewer.md:14 instructs the seat that out-of-plan edits are findings even when harmless -- the data does not contradict that (5 were produced) but not one has ever bounced a lane.
findings.evidence: task/queries/discriminators.mjs and classify.mjs; anchor verified: grep -n 'Out-of-plan edits are findings' crew/roles/reviewer.md -> line 14.

findings.summary: COUNTER-INTUITIVE, and the most important single result for rubric ORDERING: the class reviewers produce MOST is not the class that bounces. false-green (vacuous test / plan-required test absent / surviving mutation) is the largest category at 46/254 (18%) and the largest should-fix category at 19/51 (37%), but its must-fix share is 24% -- below the 47% corpus baseline. The narrower instrument (summary explicitly proves a mutation survives) gives 7/25 = 28%, also below baseline. Reading the 46: the reviewer proves the protection is missing while the shipped behaviour is correct.
findings.evidence: task/queries/classify.mjs (46 findings) and discriminators.mjs (25 findings); corpus baseline 120/254 = 47%.

findings.summary: Where findings land, must-fix share (n>=4 only): visualizer/server 6/7 (86%), scripts/factory 31/40 (78%), visualizer/web 16/21 (76%), crew 58/147 (39%), test 6/17 (35%), docs 0/4, docs/adr 0/4. They carry 54 findings, 38 (70%) must-fix, versus the 47% corpus baseline; mix is indeterminate-as-definite 14, lifecycle-clobber 10, render-join 8, unclassified 7, false-green 6. findings.summary: Finding recurrence across rounds is confounded and MUST NOT be used as a 'was it fixed' measure. Of 85 findings with a later round to compare against, 66 (78%) had their file named again next round (must-fix 36/47, should-fix 14/21, consider 16/17). A lane's scope is fixed, so the same files are re-reviewed by construction, and finding ids are minted fresh per round so they cannot be joined. The only reliable carry-forward signal is the reviewer's own prose marker (F12: 10 findings, 0 must-fix).
findings.evidence: task/queries/recurrence.mjs.

findings.summary: The proof that actually FIRES is the per-check mutation pass, and the gate is a floor rather than a filter. gate_results by name family (1879 rows, 210 lanes): gate-baseline 210 runs of which 209 correctly RED (99.5%, 1 green); gate-proof:1 rollup 187/187 red; gate-proof:1:checks:m* 1102 mutations applied across 84 lanes with 9 SURVIVORS (0.8% -- ok=1 means the gate stayed green under the mutation, i.e. the check failed to kill it); gate:r1 196/203 green (only 3.4% caught), gate:r2 66/71, gate:r3 25/25, gate:r4 13/13. Contrast F3 (review bounces 35% of first rounds) and F6 (gate green + review must-fix in 34.6% of runs): the gate is a floor, review is the filter.
findings.evidence: select gate_name, count(*), sum(ok) from gate_results grouped per family; the 9 survivors are ids 927, 1053, 1054, 1273, 1274, 1422, 1447, 1759, 1797 in lanes a0e35cf2, 1ca1ba45 x2, c4d852a3 x2, 81ca3b88, 1e170414, a8060a98, 5e40778e.

findings.summary: gate_results records no failure KIND either: violations_json is the literal string '[]' on ALL 1879 rows with no exceptions, and checks_json is only ever a one-element array of counts such as [{"total":34,"failed":2,"errored":0}] -- only three distinct string lengths (36, 37, 38 bytes) exist across the whole table. findings.summary: JSONL->DB drift measured per table: sessions 20894/20800 (94), phases 22116/22022 (94), gate_results 1891/1879 (12), review_outcomes 278/274 (4), gate_discriminations 223/220 (3); modifier_attempts, seat_teardowns, cell_failures, accept_decisions, events and intake_brakes all zero. 207 records total present in JSONL and absent from the db (the doctor's '188 keys' is a different unit and I do not claim they are comparable). 104,982 JSONL lines, 0 unparseable. The 4 drifted review rows are exactly: 193-queue d3 pass; b126-driftcheck d3 changes-needed mf=1, d5 changes-needed mf=1, d9 pass -- so b126-driftcheck is missing ENTIRELY from review_outcomes. The drift is not per-row noise; it drops whole lanes. Net effect on F1/F3 is under one percentage point, and the F2 invariant holds in the drifted rows too.

findings.summary: THE DEEPEST CONFOUND, and it limits every correlational claim in Part 2. The brief asks which findings correlate with a lane actually bouncing -- but the bounce IS the reviewer's verdict, and the verdict is a deterministic function of the same reviewer's own must-fix grade (F2, 273/274). So 'which findings correlate with a bounce' collapses to 'which findings did the reviewer grade must-fix', a single author's judgement rather than an outcome. Nothing downstream re-adjudicates that grade at scale: accept_decisions is the only re-adjudication record and it has 8 rows. There is no post-merge defect record, no revert record and no incident log in the ledger, so a must-fix that was wrong and one that was right look identical. F10/F11/F12/F13 are therefore claims about what a must-fix GRADE looks like, not validated defect-catching rates -- still the best available basis for ordering a rubric, but a rubric author must not present them as validated.
findings.evidence: F2 (273/274 determinism) + F24 (accept_decisions n=8) + absence of any outcome table in sqlite_master (22 tables enumerated; none records post-merge defects).

findings.summary: Seven questions the data CANNOT answer -- each attempted and failed on evidence, so these rubric rules must stay judgement rather than becoming checks: (1) which finding KINDS the gate catches (violations_json '[]' on all 1879 rows, checks_json counts only); (2) what a gate discrimination failure looks like (one row in 220, an infra refusal with NULL counts); (3) whether a must-fix was correct (no independent adjudication beyond 8 rows); (4) whether a bounce improved the work (round-2 pass is the same author's later verdict; recurrence confounded by fixed lane scope); (5) anything per-cell about reviews (64/274 attribution, all post-08-20, and forbidden by the brief); (6) what the 32 changes-needed envelopes with no findings array contained (recoverable only by parsing 562 review.md prose files, not attempted -- so every Part 2 count is a count over the 74% that opted in); (7) whether seat teardown ever went badly (one value in every column of 569 rows).
findings.evidence: F20, F17, F24/F28, F3/F16, F26, F8, F23 respectively.

findings.summary: RUBRIC ORDERING implied by the evidence, ranked by measured must-fix yield with denominators (ordering is the evidence; absolute rates carry F28): (1) demand a counterexample -- state -> wrong observable in one short sentence [74% vs 20%, n=254; must-fix median 143 chars vs consider 273]; (2) an indeterminate state collapsed into a definite one -- EPERM/EINVAL/unknown read as dead, absent read as zero [60%, n=50]; (3) lifecycle and clobber -- terminal envelope overwritten, orphaned fork, settled seat re-settled [63%, n=32]; (4) the degradation path and optional instrumentation becoming load-bearing [77%, n=13]; (5) hostile CLI/API input -- empty flag, trailing flag, __proto__, Symbol, giant int, URL userinfo, prefix slicing [57%, n=21]; (6) rendering that joins by array position or drops rows on duplicate keys [71%, n=14]; (7) vacuous tests / surviving mutations -- KEEP the rule but rank it should-fix by default [24-28%, n=46, below the 47% baseline]; (8) plan conformance and out-of-plan edits [25% n=20; out-of-plan specifically 0 of 5]; (9) stale comments/docs/READMEs/charters [0 of 23]; (10) carried-forward findings [0 of 10]. Two framing facts: the gate does NOT pre-clear mechanical defects (gate:r1 green 96.6% yet review finds a must-fix in 34.6% of green-gate runs), and half of reviews correctly find nothing (140/269) -- so pressuring the seat toward a minimum finding count would optimise against the measured baseline.
findings.evidence: Composite of F5, F6, F9, F10, F11, F12, F13, F19; the full table with denominators is findings.md Part 7.

findings.summary: CORRECTION TO STANDING MEMORY. Memory records that review_outcomes' must_fix/should_fix/consider are '0% null and read by NOTHING'. The first half is confirmed exactly. The second half is FALSE as of this commit -- three live readers: (a) crew/escalation-policy.mjs:180-181, regrantVerdict() filters review rows on Number.isInteger(row.must_fix) then requires the count sequence to be monotonically non-increasing with a last value <= 1 (condition 'must-fix-converging', line 200), so the count drives whether an escalated run is granted extra rounds -- load-bearing; (b) scripts/factory/ledger.mjs:2553 and :3843, gateReviewGap()/the gate-review-gap verb compute MAX(must_fix) per run, which is the ADR-030 gate-adequacy metric and exactly the number in F6; (c) the visualizer renders it per round -- ReviewPanel.svelte:13, trace.js:139, panels.js:246, shape.mjs:249, ledger-feed.mjs:80. Corrected form: the counts are 0% null, are read by the regrant policy, the gate-adequacy readout and the visualizer, and carry almost no information beyond the verdict itself (F2) -- the finding KINDS are what nothing reads, because nothing records them (F7).
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'must_fix' crew scripts visualizer docs (excluding tests); anchors re-verified individually: grep -n 'must-fix-converging' crew/escalation-policy.mjs -> 4, 200; grep -n 'function gateReviewGap' scripts/factory/ledger.mjs -> 2547.

findings.summary: The disk envelope corpus is a STRICT SUPERSET of the ledger's review history, which explains the 194-vs-227 lane gap without any sampling assumption: all 191 ledger slugs carrying a review appear on disk, and 36 disk slugs have no ledger review row at all (crew-hygiene, plan-viewer, alloc, realio, herdr-spike, pi-spike, headless-spike, ...). Spot-checked file mtimes put those at 2026-08-13/14, before review_outcomes' first row at 2026-08-14T23:15:59.978Z -- they predate the table. Use the ledger from 08-15 onward and the disk for the whole history.
findings.evidence: task/queries/laneoverlap.mjs -- in both 191, disk-only 36 (full list printed), ledger-only 0; stat -f %Sm on one envelope per spot-checked lane.
